claim: Crypto-funded card spend rose from ~$100M/month in early 2023 to ~$1.5B/month by late 2025, a ~15x increase, annualizing to ~$18B.
quoted_support: monthly crypto card spend rose from roughly $100M in early 2023 to about $1.5B by late 2025, implying an annualized ~$18B, around 15x growth.

claim: Stablecoin-linked card spending is not merchant crypto acceptance but stablecoin-funded cards riding existing card network rails — direct evidence the mechanism is absorption, not bypass.
quoted_support: This is not merchants “accepting crypto.” It is stablecoin-funded cards riding existing card networks.

claim: Visa carries over 90% of on-chain crypto card transaction volume despite both Visa and Mastercard supporting 130+ crypto card programs, due to early alignment with crypto-native issuers.
stance_target: competitive dynamics between card networks in stablecoin absorption
quoted_support: Visa dominates the rails: Visa carries >90% of on-chain crypto card volume despite both Visa and Mastercard supporting 130+ crypto card programs.

claim: Full-stack crypto-native issuers (Rain, Reap) became Visa principal members, capturing interchange/FX/reserve-yield economics; Rain scaled ~38x to over $3B annualized, Reap over $6B annualized.
stance_target: where value accrues in the stablecoin-card stack
quoted_support: Rain scaled sharply in 2025 (reported ~38x) to >$3B annualized after direct Visa membership; Reap is reported at >$6B annualized, skewing toward corporate spend.

claim: The 2026 base case for stablecoin cards is continued infrastructure maturation and steady growth, not an abrupt shift to fully crypto-native merchant payments.
quoted_support: Base case: continued infrastructure maturation and steady growth, not an abrupt shift to fully crypto-native merchant payments.

claim: Direct merchant stablecoin acceptance remains limited due to disputes, compliance, and merchant tooling gaps; stablecoins increasingly function as a settlement back-end rather than the checkout experience.
quoted_support: Stablecoins are the back-end, not the checkout: Direct merchant stablecoin acceptance remains limited due to disputes, compliance, and merchant tooling.
